o: Lord, eternal God, I praise You as I begin this day. Thank You, because Your promises do not fail and Your faithfulness is renewed every morning. There are things in my life I am still waiting for, and sometimes I grow impatient. Today I want to learn to wait on You, like the watchman who watches for the dawn, with the certainty that the light always comes in the end. Thank You for every promise fulfilled in my life.

Give me a patient heart, attentive to Your voice. Teach me not to be discouraged when the answers delay, nor to doubt when the road seems long. You know the times and You know what is best for me. Increase my faith, Lord, and help me rest in Your plans, even if I do not fully understand them. May hope fill my mind and my home.

Bless today my work, my family and every person I will meet. May my words bring peace and my actions show Your love. Protect me from any haste that takes me away from You and remind me that You are with me at every step. Accompany those who wait for a healing, a job or a reconciliation, and give them strength to keep trusting. Thank You for Your kindness. May Your Spirit guide me today. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: In Jerusalem there lived a man named Simeon. Luke describes him as righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and says that the Holy Spirit was upon him. Moreover, it had been revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ. This probably meant many years of waiting, though we are not told how many. His life shows us that waiting on God is a way of trusting him.

One day, led by the Spirit, Simeon went to the temple. Just at that moment, Mary and Joseph came in with the child Jesus to do what the law required. Among so many people passing through the temple that day, Simeon knew how to recognize the Savior. He took the child in his arms and blessed God with words we still repeat: “Lord, now you are letting your servant depart in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation.”

Simeon also spoke to Mary and Joseph, and told them that this child would be a light to enlighten the nations and the glory of Israel, God's people. The parents marveled at what was said about him. After that, Luke tells us that the prophetess Anna, an elderly woman who served God in the temple with fasting and prayers, gave thanks to God and spoke about the child to all who were waiting for redemption.

The story of Simeon teaches us that waiting on God is never in vain. He sustained his servant for years, and when the moment came, Simeon held in his arms the answer to his hope. God fulfills what he promises, and his times are perfect. Today, we can learn from Simeon to wait in peace, to recognize Jesus and to give thanks even before we have seen everything fulfilled.
m.c: May this day find you trusting in the Lord, with a firm step and a serene heart. He is faithful and fulfills all he promises, even when you do not yet see it. Walk in peace, for his mercy surrounds you and his light illuminates your path today.
m: Waiting is one of the hardest tasks in life. Simeon waited, and we do not know for how long. Perhaps he saw many days pass without seeing the promise fulfilled. Yet he did not become embittered and did not stop going to the temple. His waiting was filled with communion with God and attention to the voice of the Spirit, and that made it fruitful.

The psalmist writes that his soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning. The watchman knows the dawn will come, because it always has. This is the kind of hope God invites us to have: not a vague illusion, but a firm trust in someone who has proven his faithfulness. What you are waiting for today is in the hands of the one who never fails.

Notice also how Simeon recognized Jesus. He was attentive. Often God acts in the midst of the ordinary, and one who is hurried or distracted does not notice. Today, in the midst of your tasks, open your eyes to the small signs of God's goodness: a kind word, a door that opens, a moment of calm. Whoever waits attentively discovers that God is already at work.

For today, here is what I suggest. Make a short list of what you are waiting for from God and present it in prayer, saying sincerely: “I trust in you.” While you wait, serve someone, for waiting grows light when it is devoted to blessing. And at the end of the day, note one sign of God's faithfulness that you noticed. You will see how your faith grows.

o: Merciful Lord, at nightfall, I thank You for this day You have given me. Thank You for health, for work, for food and for the people who helped me. I also thank You for the opportunities to do good that You placed before me, even though I did not always know how to seize them as I should. Blessed are You for Your faithfulness.

Forgive me for the times I passed by on my way, busy with my own affairs, without seeing the need of others. Teach me to have the compassion Jesus had, who draws near to the wounded and lifts them up. Give me eyes to see, hands to help and a heart that does not tire of loving. May my home be a place of peace and unity, and may my words always be words of blessing.

I place in Your hands the burdens of this day and everything I could not settle. Take care of those who suffer, those who are far from home and those who felt forgotten today. Give them consolation and send someone to help them, as You sent the Samaritan. Grant me peaceful sleep and wake me tomorrow with a renewed desire to serve You. Thank You for Your constant love. Give me deep rest. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: A lawyer asked Jesus who his neighbor was, and the Lord answered with a story that Luke preserved in his Gospel. A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, wounded him and left him half dead by the roadside. It was a lonely and dangerous route, and the man could not help himself. He lay there, in need of someone to have compassion on him.

A priest happened to be going down that road and, seeing the wounded man, passed by on the other side. Soon after, a Levite also came by, and did the same. Both knew God's law and served in the temple, but they did not stop. Then a Samaritan came along, a man from a people the Jews of that time often despised. When he saw him, Luke says, he had compassion.

The Samaritan went to him, bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal and brought him to an inn, where he took care of him. The next day he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper and said: “Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.” It was no small service; he gave his time, his money and his care.

Jesus then asked the lawyer which of the three seemed to him to have been a neighbor to the wounded man. He answered: “The one who showed him mercy.” And Jesus said to him: “Go and do likewise.” In this way, he taught us that being a neighbor does not depend on who is in need, but on having a heart that lets itself be moved to help.
t.c: When the light of this day goes out, give the Lord your weariness and the burdens you have carried, for he cares for you. Sleep quietly, with the peace of one who knows he is not alone. May his goodness wrap around you all night long and may you wake tomorrow in calm.
m: The parable of the good Samaritan begins with a question we all ask ourselves in one way or another: whom must I help? Jesus turned the question around. He did not speak of who deserves to be helped, but of who becomes the neighbor. He invites us to look differently at those around us, especially those who suffer and have no one to care for them.

Notice what the Samaritan did. He did not have the same advantages as the priest or the Levite, and yet he is the one who stopped. God's compassion was shown in concrete action: bandaging, carrying, bringing, paying and returning. Faith becomes visible when love is translated into practical gestures, even small and simple ones.

The psalmist says how good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell together in unity. When we help others, unity also grows in the family, in the church and in the neighborhood. A home where the weary are cared for and the suffering are listened to is a place where God pours out his blessing. Harmony is not born by chance, but from daily decisions of love.

Before sleeping, review your day with these questions. Whom could I have helped without having done so? Ask God's forgiveness and decide to do it tomorrow. Whom did I help, even with little? Give thanks for that opportunity. And think of a specific person you could call, visit or encourage in the coming days. God will give you the means and the opportunity.
